## Quality review

Candidate: [`85206b1c22dab78e8379d7a10e2f2b9ac31af9c6`](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/commit/85206b1c22dab78e8379d7a10e2f2b9ac31af9c6).
Base: [`845cec3060b0880cd27c36047f1da57a1c3772ba`](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/commit/845cec3060b0880cd27c36047f1da57a1c3772ba).
**T2 Need architect.** Architecture: T2: declarations changed in 2 public
modules; 5 registry views edited. The final local checker is eligible with no
blockers. Overall merge was **eligible** and the approved candidate is now merged. The owner directly approved this exact head as architect, accepted the stated S1 limits for the internal rollout, and approved the complete notice package and existing-organization disposition. [Exact human answers and scope](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/a7284b0c4dc02a8c7cd7958cfdc4a11ce4adee89/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/approvals/owner-approval.json). Agent review is separate from this human approval. Approved publication and deployment are complete. Deployed delivery verification remains pending; see [current rollout status](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/a99440ea6cf302abc04e0de11e630dcd12d37427/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/postmerge/progress-before-unlock.json).

**Tier reasons and impact.** T2 reasons are
`architecture.declarations_changed` for `destination-settings-service.ts`
(+3 −1 declaration lines) and `audit-send.ts` (+1),
`architecture.registry_view_changed` for five edited views, and `impact.contract`.
T1 reasons are `protected_paths.deploy_and_data` for
`Dockerfile.hosted.dockerignore` and `impact.sensitiveBehavior`. All six reasons
are retained; the highest tier controls. No component set, component dependency,
runtime process or container is added; System logging keeps its separate owner
and transport. The final checker reports no undeclared facts, no blockers and no
exception use. [Final checker](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/quality/pr-review.json).

The [committed impact declaration](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/85206b1c22dab78e8379d7a10e2f2b9ac31af9c6/.pr-impact.json) and [stamped input](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/quality/impact.json) describe this complete candidate against its actual main base.

The checker's seven informational notes each have a disposition: 48 public
modules with two changed snapshots are verified declaration scope;
`OtlpAuditSender` is touched with declarations unchanged, so its type contract
adds no third declaration fact. Its three changed imports (`audit-send`,
`public-audit-destination`, `otlp-audit-request`) still need semantic review:
they carry and validate the optional dataset through the existing sender, as
covered by the authority, header and lifetime review below. Size notes are
436 production lines versus 400 and 3,223 total non-generated lines versus 1,500.
The frozen legal literal bundle, canonical legal data and operational/review
documents explain much of this volume; the small routing field remains within
existing owners. The metric and Habit Hooks reviews retain specific cohesion
reasons rather than extract code merely to reduce size. These are notes, not
extra human tiers. The final checker also warns that local eligibility is
preliminary: the manager must verify current checks, holds and human approval.

**Policy answers.** The changed client/operator promise is one optional saved
Axiom dataset, forwarded only from the authorized current tenant/revision. Blank
or omitted dataset retains generic OTLP behavior. Save remains atomic; Test does
not save or enable. Dataset-only edits advance revision, stale queued work is
dropped, and already-authorized in-flight work may finish. Header syntax is
validated at both Admin and sender boundaries before remote work. The existing
Admin, Origin/CSRF, tenant predicates, public-address/DNS/pinned peer and verified
TLS rules remain. Token retention requires unchanged endpoint/auth; auth None clears
the token. Dataset and credentials remain outside event bodies and System settings.
The new bundle changes displayed legal versions/hashes, with one unchecked
creator checkbox and stale-form refusal. Existing acceptance records are kept;
no new acceptance by existing users is claimed.

The image adds the three canonical v3 inputs required by its exact-byte tests.
Stored settings add nullable `axiom_dataset`; apply the additive migration before
the new adapter. Old code can read its original columns but ignores the dataset
and cannot perform direct Axiom routing. Disable export before rollback to that
code and retain the schema and encryption key; schema compatibility alone does
not prove equivalent delivery. No new dependency or production System exporter
is introduced. Recovery/backup moves to future Slice 4 by owner instruction;
this slice has no settings backup. Export remains bounded best effort with
possible loss/duplicates and no event history/replay.

**Metrics.** The complete 185e372a analysis finished all four stages: retained
Delta/Review/CRAP goal misses (exit 1), Architecture pass. Ten existing production
MI misses and one high/eight medium findings each have a specific retained reason
in [metric dispositions](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/metrics-dispositions.md); no mechanical
extraction is justified. The high integration test keeps the actual queued
revision/dataset oracle visible. The 346-line legal bundle is frozen literal
data, not equivalent branching complexity. Final process and standalone CRAP retain exit 1 for those raw goal misses; the
final checker accepts the applicable goals and reports no exception use.
[Final process](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/quality/process.md),
[CRAP rows](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/quality/crap.json),
[review data](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/quality/review.json).

Measured changed/new CRAP rows meet applicable hard goals. The two changed target
suggestions, 17.1 and 15.002737575, remain below 30. Two source coverage unknowns
remain explicit: changed `requestAuditExport` and conservatively new Pg close
closure, each one path. Emitted calls do not supply missing source identity;
the unchanged Pg closure cannot be paired uniquely and was not invoked by unit
coverage. Both worst-case ranges [1,2] prove even the new goal under the checker;
no new exception is needed. The final JSON keeps coverage unknown, and the
checker explicitly confirms both bound passes. Preserve the process's unknown
status and exit 1. The one unchanged unknown hosted closure stays
`unchanged by this PR`. [Complete source analysis](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/metrics-source-185e372a-process.md),
[raw review](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/metrics-source-185e372a-review.json).

Verified coverage was captured at 185e372a, for both complete unit parts, with
source/input/runtime/compiler and suite fingerprints. Final reuse after the
history commit passed compatibility checks; the capture is not relabelled.
Base CRAP derived with head coverage is an estimate; no measured base coverage
is claimed. The native dependency report retains the same unresolved CSS asset import at both revisions; it cannot prove a complete graph from that evidence alone. Global and component
unknowns remain; no component average proves a function goal. Worker PG/Collector
runs have limited individual-file/chronological provenance, not full head-bound
input manifests. [Validation](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/pull/248#issuecomment-6390817756)
keeps complete gate, failure/retry and coverage provenance.

**Habit Hooks and manual review.** All 92 retained locations have reasons:
10 complexity, 15 non-null assertions, three parameter counts, 59 comments and
five sizes. The one weak test setup was fixed with `assert.ok(current)`, then
passed its 39-case rerun and the complete gates. The final committed Hook rerun
has the same 92 findings, with only the oversized-list order changed. Snooze
remains `[]`.
[Each disposition](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/habit-review.md).
The global staged whitespace check exited 2 with 62 individually reviewed
intentional findings: 54 unified-diff context markers and eight frozen legal
Markdown hard breaks. Remaining paths passed the scoped check, exit 0; this is
not a blanket global pass. [Every whitespace reason](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/whitespace-review.json).

<details>
<summary>Architecture provenance and review</summary>

All 13 registry diagrams were inventoried; views 1,2,6,7,13 changed. The focused
L3 and changed registry views were parsed, rendered and inspected at 800px;
the manager accepted all six images. The single authoritative comparison remains
in the main description. [Versioned review](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/architecture/v4/review.md)
and [manifest](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/architecture/v4/candidate-manifest.json) retain
actual compared code, registry and diagram bytes. Versions 1–3 preserve the earlier reviews; v4 binds all 60 changed files and the full source tree to the committed candidate. Diagram sources and all six renders are byte-identical. The final binding in
[manager record](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/manager-review-final.json) binds the review
to the final candidate without relabelling the earlier capture.
L4 is omitted because L3 plus the authority/payload/revision/lifetime notes answer
the strongest changed callable contract, `AuditDestination.axiomDataset`.
No test-helper API creates a production L4 requirement. The Docker-context and
queued-forwarding findings are fixed; no production correctness finding remains
in that reviewed scope. No new architecture decision record was requested; the optional field extends the existing destination contract and runtime roles. The observed client-to-pooler TLS limit remains explicit in v4. This does not prove deployment or notice approval.

</details>

Prior published evidence and approval history remain in the
[archived initial report](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/blob/257baca8b985083e6a7f3ab7c7c3e40642a445c0/ast-report/s2-04-rollout/review-draft/pr248-initial-evidence.json).

marketing.body:
Public guides still described personal User workspaces, Google sign-in, and no customer Audit export. This change describes the deployed organization signup and invitation flow, email/password sign-in, internal System logs, and optional Admin-configured Audit export. It also removes the homepage claim that files wait for human approval.

The Audit guide explains atomic Save/enable, saved Test, custom receiver URLs, direct Axiom routing, capture limits, pattern redaction, best-effort delivery, destination retention, and no Slice 2 backups. Member removal, role changes, MFA and SSO are not presented as shipped features.

The approved Terms, Privacy and their wrappers remain byte-identical to main. Prices, CTA behavior, layout, styles and dependencies are unchanged. No production callable contract or architecture boundary changes.

Validation: Node 24.20.0 `npm run check` passed all 62 existing tests, typecheck and build.
